div.head: II Ew II Ew. 1
div.ab: Eadweard cyning mid his witan, ða hy æt Exceastre wæron, smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mehte, ðone hit ær ðæm wæs; forðam him ðuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, ðonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

Eadweard cyning myngode his wytan, þa hy æt Exanceastre wæron, þæt hy smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mæhte, þonne hit ær ðam wæs; forðam him þuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, þonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

Eadwardus rex admonuit omnes sapientes suos, quando fuerunt Exonie, ut inuestigarent simul et quererent, quomodo pax eorum melior esse posset, quam antea fuit; quia uisum est ei, quod hoc mediocrius impletum sit, quam deceret, et quam antea precepisset.

[Be fryþe.] [Ld] Eadweard cyning myngode his wytan, þa hy æt Exanceastre wæron, þæt hy smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mæhte, þonne hit ær ðæm wæs; forðam him þuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, þonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

King Edward exhorted all his councillors, when they were at Exeter, to consider how the public peace for which they were responsible could be kept better than it had been, because it seemed to him that the previous orders had not been carried out so well as they ought to have been.

(Von öffentlicher Sicherheit. Ld) König Eadward ermahnte seine Witan, als sie zu Exeter waren, dass sie alle berathschlagen möchten, wie ihre öffentliche Sicherheit besser werden könne, als es vordem war; denn ihm schien, dass jenes, was er früher geboten hatte, minder, als es sich gebührte, erfüllt wäre.

(Of public security. Ld) King Edward exhorted his witan, when they were at Exeter, that they should all deliberate how their public security might become better than it was before; for it seemed to him that what he had commanded earlier was fulfilled less than was fitting.
